check: describe command('grep -rqE \'^[^#]*\bpam_unix\\.so\b[^#]*\bnullok\' /etc/pam.d/ 2>/dev/null && echo ko || echo ok') do

remediation.command:
# Remove 'nullok' (allow empty passwords) from pam_unix. Keep a root session open while testing.
sed -ri 's/\bnullok\b//g' /etc/pam.d/common-auth /etc/pam.d/common-password
# verify a normal login still works in another session
remediation.reason: editing the PAM stack can lock you out — verify auth in a SECOND session before logout

title.en: Prevent Login to Accounts With Empty Password
title.fr: Prevent Login to Accounts With Empty Password

rationale.en: If an account has an empty password, anyone could log in and run commands with the privileges of that account. Accounts with empty passwords should never be used in operational environments.
rationale.fr: If an account has an empty password, anyone could log in and run commands with the privileges of that account. Accounts with empty passwords should never be used in operational environments.
